capabilities.compatibility: Keep single and multiple selection modes, existing document-generator values, the attach/setValue/setDisabled contract, and the apex:client-change/open/error events during migration. Sorting, incremental paging, recents, grouping, and highlighting are additive presentation features; client choices still resolve through the case-management client archive.
Preserve option labels and phone metadata. Mail member menus read the same suohan_lawyers IDs and names, without a separate member directory.
Keep the existing macOS keychain service/account stable so meeting-room booking and chapter applications share credentials and token refresh behavior.
Case management remains authoritative.

All active-case candidate menus use ApexCasePicker.attach with popup or inline presentation and single or multiple selection. Keep case IDs, full series-child titles, selection callbacks, optional free-text project names, and existing business actions. Sorting and recent selections are shared across pages; client grouping lists multi-client cases under each client. The case-lookup API keeps items and adds bounded offset pagination (has_more, next_offset) plus folder_bound flags; no folder paths are disclosed. Consumers load every page before sorting and render at most 60 additional rows per expansion. Document generators consume case context from their launch URL rather than offering a separate case menu.
Preserve native input values in YYYY-MM-DD form.

Keep light, dark, and user color theme propagation across iframes. A saved theme value of dark or light takes priority across all pages and browser tabs; when no explicit value is saved, initialize and react to system appearance through prefers-color-scheme. Shared color-theme.css and color-theme.js are loaded by child pages; brand accents use kb-theme or apex-accent tokens while destructive and status colors stay semantic.

The existing single and bulk article DELETE endpoints still accept the same requests and report success, but now move article rows and cascading dependencies into recoverable snapshots. Each snapshot expires 30 days after its own deletion time. The background task and trash-list reads purge expired snapshots. Restoring preserves the original article ID and notes, while stale links to separately removed records may be skipped and reported. Uploaded source files remain untouched.

One transparent PNG or WebP logo is shared across color themes. Dark UI surfaces use a cached one-time recolor that lightens neutral strokes, preserves red strokes, and adds a small static red halo; the original source remains unchanged for light mode and the Dock icon. The current logo remains in localStorage for synchronous launch rendering; uploaded history is in IndexedDB. Legacy color-theme logo keys migrate once to history. The global tab bar brand button replaces the visible main tab and invokes the same switchTab('main') action; mobile retains its separate home button. The native brandIcon handler accepts only local application pages and changes the running Dock icon. The packaged Stella icon is built from the approved brand asset; when that same artwork is selected, including a re-encoded copy, the running Dock reuses the bundled icns. Other uploads are rendered with the same inset rounded canvas and packaged through the same multiresolution iconset pipeline before the running Dock icon changes. Keep the existing bundle identifier so WebKit data and macOS permissions remain available. The native client publishes its active logo into ignored data/mobile-brand.json; authenticated settings changes also publish it. Public GET /api/brand and /brand-logo.png contain only branding, while PUT /api/brand requires existing authentication. Mobile clients retain the last logo locally for offline startup, refresh it on connection and foreground, and render dark variants with the shared adapter. Installation icon responses use a white square canvas without a second rounded mask and revalidate instead of retaining a one-day cache. Manifest id remains /case-manager and start_url is /; existing iOS home icons may require re-adding the shortcut. Shell v232 refreshes branding without deleting case caches or pending operations.

Preserve Finder copy/paste, upload, download, and private-mode restrictions. Local file list and search responses may add Finder tag metadata; the case-files page and AI file picker render the seven macOS tag colors, while the case-files context menu may update the selected file or folder's Finder tag color and recursively apply it to descendants when a folder is selected. Scanner case imports reuse store_case_file with download_material under #下载材料, retain source metadata and the existing import response, and validate the binding before retrieval and again at write. Judicial-delivery archive folders default to #Stella电子送达归档 and the Important/red Finder tag on creation or legacy migration; reuse the Finder metadata helpers, preserve other tags and later user edits, and do not tag descendants by default.

Existing business download/export routes remain compatible. Unified authenticated metadata is atomically persisted under runtime data, with bounded 2000-record history and at most three managed jobs. Seven sources share honest real-byte/unknown-size progress and case/path context; court dossiers retain their durable executor. Invoice scans cover all selectable IMAP folders with account/folder-scoped caches and paths, bounded complete-range continuation, isolated invoice summaries and UIDVALIDITY reset handling; signed amounts and explicit invoice identity drive selection/totals; exports preserve all selected files within a documented bound and serialize history repair/write; browser view revisions reject stale account responses; scan warnings and timeouts propagate as partial completion to downloads and monthly collection. Mail invoice vs case vs other is explicit; case writes require confirmation and currently available folder binding. Normal mail collection no longer writes into invoice folders. Legacy browser history imports idempotently and only locates exact existing Downloads basenames, never infers a case. File paths cannot be assigned by client PATCH; native user-selected paths must match a known downloaded artifact byte for byte. Native ZIP transfers retain streaming without a browser memory ceiling. Cleaning completed records never deletes files or hides unassigned case materials. Native WKDownload byte observations report actual save-panel paths; apex:open-download-source version 1 routes only requests from a registered download-center frame to an allowlisted existing feature; relaunch is required to activate a rebuilt native shell. New progress assets are data-free public shell resources; business endpoints remain authenticated.
Keep record IDs routable from macOS notifications.

New events use the apex:* namespace and include a version when their payload is not trivial. The archive picker inside case-files uses apex:archive-picker-ready, apex:archive-selection, and apex:archive-assign-request with version 1, caseId, and relative file paths; the archive workbench replies with apex:archive-status or apex:archive-clear-selection for the same caseId. Both frames check same origin and the expected source frame. Knowledge center uses apex:knowledge-prefill-ask with version 1 and question; the parent checks same origin and the source knowledge tab iframe before filling AI Ask. apex:open-court-downloads carries version 1 and optional jobId; the main host validates same origin and a court-online or download-center source iframe before opening the progress tab.

The apex:page-visibility message is version 1; host tab selection is independent from document visibility, so foreground recovery resumes only selected pages; overview cards remain visible without CSS entry animations; inactive pages may pause work but must preserve drafts. Low-risk read-only pages may be hibernated after their state is captured; editors, recordings, uploads, CAPTCHA flows and other unsafe pages remain mounted until they implement an explicit snapshot contract.

The public shell contains no case data. Keep the Service Worker scope and /case-manager entry stable, preserve the legal-kb-case-manager IndexedDB schema and pending case-operation queue, validate shell responses before caching, and never clear user data during shell repair. Verified top-level /case-manager navigation enters /?workspace=cases, reusing the existing main tab host and mobile floating navigation; iframe case navigation is never redirected. The public /app-shell endpoint exposes only source UI markup, and its required static assets are public; business APIs remain authenticated. Shell installation must finish preparing the main host even for a fresh signed-out standalone data store. Manifest start_url is / while its identity remains /case-manager. Standalone legacy case HTML enters /?workspace=cases even before a worker controls the page. A same-origin case iframe with expired authentication navigates its parent app to login. The main shell and its versioned assets are prepared independently of browser cookies, and a home-ready marker is published only after every asset succeeds. Offline root navigation ignores query parameters and uses a verified home cache; online login responses remain authoritative.

articles.domains remains the top-level JSON list. GET /api/domains keeps domain and count fields and adds id and children. Article list and detail responses add subcategories with id, name, parent_id and domain alongside subcategory_ids; main article cards and both reader metadata bars display confirmed child labels, with cached catalog resolution for older offline snapshots. Both readers keep source, author, date and label editing outside the collapsible classification labels, visible in both disclosure states with wrapping on narrow screens. Main cards and both reader metadata bars share a single-line label disclosure, showing an expand/collapse button only for overflow and adapting to container resizing. Rules cover every predefined domain and known historical roots, with AI fallback evaluated per domain; migration 16 backfills historical child-topic evidence without changing article assignments. Rules and configured AI discover child suggestions from new and historical articles; known related phrases are consolidated into reusable topics, and automatic proposals enter the review list and can be approved only when at least two distinct articles support a concise topic. Original single-article proposals remain stored. No suggestion enters the approved taxonomy without confirmation. User-selected and excluded classifications and child order survive automatic re-evaluation; source URLs remain article metadata. Deleting a child taxonomy node removes only its article associations, preserves the articles, and suppresses future automatic proposals with the same name under that parent; explicit manual creation clears the suppression. Root deletion remains a separate flow. The unified directory manager owns professional/custom/author editing, with explicit drag handles, insertion boundaries, edge scrolling and Alt/Option keyboard ordering; root dragging temporarily hides child rows and restores them on drop or cancellation without changing expansion preferences; legacy open functions remain adapters. Child rename preserves IDs, keywords and article associations and suppresses old automatic proposals. Reorder requests validate a complete current visible collection and return 409 atomically on duplicates or stale IDs. Offline article snapshot v3 adds subcategory_ids and classification_status without changing IndexedDB keys; older snapshots remain usable for general browsing, but child/pending filters require v3 and the relevant fields. Saved views accept optional subcategoryId, clear absent or deleted child IDs, and retain the parent domain. Expansion mode and paths use the safely parsed legal_kb_directory_state_v1 preference; hovering a root reveals its next level, while hovering a specific child reveals only its own descendants after pointer intent detection; search expansion is temporary. Reclassification preview adds has_changes and subcategory_add/remove by comparing effective assignments, respecting manual selections and exclusions. Matching an existing child or requesting AI alone is not a change. Batched apply skips unchanged articles and adds scanned alongside processed and next_after_id.

Collect aggregate local metrics only; never retain URLs with queries, request bodies, client names, file paths, or case content. Additive metrics may include current and peak memory, aggregate child-process usage, thread/task counts, hibernated-page counts, and coarse case-manager startup stage/timing; child command-line arguments are never collected.

CC2API is additive. cc2api: model IDs use the official Claude Code headless client for Claude Code-only key groups and normalize JSON results into the existing choices contract. The pinned client lives in ignored data/cc2api-runtime; scripts/install_cc2api_runtime.py installs it. Per-call temporary configuration, bare mode, no built-in or MCP tools, and no session persistence isolate the client. Cancellation and timeout kill the child. Keys remain in private config and child environment only. Existing defaults and fallback behavior remain compatible. Direct modes direct_ai and direct_ai_web return before KB/MCP routing, use separate conversation history, and reuse the public web adapter from case_files for every provider. Direct web mode plans bounded queries with current Shanghai date and recent user context, retrieves through a shared multi-engine adapter, checks entity/topic relevance, follows validated HTTP/meta redirects, and records retrieval time. Only actual relevant public web results are returned as external_sources; search failure is explicit and the retrieval budget is 45 seconds. New Doubao 2.1 0915 model IDs are additive and require Ark activation; the stable Mini alias now uses verified 260428.

data_source: Case ownership graph: case_manager_*/case_archive_*, tables with case_id/linked_case_id/matched_case_id, recursive foreign-key descendants, project-linked articles only
capabilities.compatibility: Reuses the existing AI chat DOM, models, exports and request cancellation. CASE_AI is a separate singleton tab; case_database has isolated conversation history and excludes unrelated KB, web, MCP and skills. SQL authorizer permits only case-related tables and non-secret columns, bounded read queries and aggregates on a consistent SQLite snapshot. All synced court-online records, including unmatched cases, filing audits, hearings, delivery messages and raw JSON fields are available; sync timestamps and multiple accounts must be distinguished. Case-linked research projects, ledgers, memo entries, notes, questions, search runs, personal income, reading records and project-linked articles are available through recursive ownership discovery. All-case snapshots retain unlinked court records but remove unbound research and unrelated articles. AI histories and research answers are secondary working records, not verified facts. Focused requests preload project-owned memo/ledger/notes text with citation links before model planning; large results and long text require pagination. Basic case memo is distinct from drawer memo entries. Final JSON answer envelopes are unwrapped on every backend path; historical envelopes are normalized for rendering, copying and export. No live portal fetch or database writes. Existing AI_ASK sources remain compatible. Specific case evidence carries case_links and opens a case_id deep link in the shared case detail drawer. Old clipped JSON sources are normalized at display time; case-only controls are hidden and tables retain readable minimum column widths. Case-only shortcuts prefill editable questions without sending requests or mutating case data. Active/archived and 7/30/90-day controls affect generated questions only; unmatched court records remain a separate review list. Empty conversations show the welcome shortcuts only. After the first message, the shortcuts move to a collapsible composer toolbar; returning to an empty conversation or leaving case mode removes it. Styles remain scoped to the case AI workspace in the existing stylesheet, preserving offline shell asset paths. Optional caseId/caseTitle in the case_database context separate focused histories and add a case-specific instruction to every request without changing the read-only query API. POST /api/ask accepts optional focus_case_id for case_database. Focused requests materialize a read-only in-memory snapshot containing only the selected case, actual series children and explicitly owned records (including foreign-key descendants); unfiltered SQL and aggregates cannot reach other cases. Unlinked court records and tables without an ownership path are unavailable in this scope and require separate review. Timeline requests use structured cited events, sorted by validated dates with unknown dates and system records in separate sections. The focus and todo review dialogs reuse ApexCasePicker. Answer excerpts can prefill editable notes; only explicit draft confirmation calls the existing POST /api/case-manager/todos, with no inferred dates or completion status.

Single-user local saved memories are separate from chat history. Additive memory_enabled form field defaults true for all AI workspace scopes including attachments. Context is personalization data, never legal evidence or executable instructions. Anchored remember/forget/list commands are local; conservative auto-save reads only current first-person name/preference statements after a successful answer. Settings default enabled/auto_save true. Global disable and per-request no-memory stop reading and capture; disabling retains records. Deleting chat never deletes memories; no old chat or documents are mined. Max 100 entries of 500 characters. Revision guard prevents in-flight auto-save from reversing a manual edit, deletion or settings change. Nested authoritative file retrieval opts out of personalization; updated home-shell cache includes the new data-free CSS/JS assets. Existing numbered migration backup path is reused.

Packaging only; existing runtime and APIs stay unchanged. No existing database, uploads, financial records, local credentials, browser sessions, user Skills or Git history. Team defaults retained by explicit user authorization. Original sample articles and fictional cases seed once; deleted examples never return. Dedicated loopback port and runtime/config directories. Default preview branding uses the shipped Stella wordmark. Ad-hoc signed Apple Silicon app; no notarization claimed.

Existing synchronous download route remains compatible, with additive progress result and authenticated progress GET. Actual decoded byte counts, unknown-size indeterminate state, per-file saved/failed counters and honest partial failure. Bounded in-memory snapshots, duplicate download prevention and serial polling only in visible active drawer. Restart clears progress; business files and database are unchanged.

Additive per-record shortcuts for todos, hearings, preservations and appeals. No case folder binding changes or file copies; exclusive foreign keys cascade metadata only. Authenticated local desktop access remains allowed in private mode; loopback peer/target, local Origin and no proxy forwarding headers are required. Authentication stays in middleware. Permission-denied 403 retains its reason without a login redirect; 401 and login HTML still redirect. Picker cancellation does not create a binding. List shortcuts open a single valid binding directly, show an anchored keyboard-accessible picker for multiple or missing bindings, and enter binding management only when unbound. Scoped reminder actions stay on one row with intact hit areas in a fixed-width column; content columns share the remaining width and narrow desktop panes scroll horizontally. Case actions remain compatible. Missing or changed-kind paths never launch; open validates ownership by both record and link ID.

Additive local member metadata scoped by account/folder/UID, checked against summary date/from/subject to avoid reused UID labels. Atomic bulk writes; surviving cache eviction and restart. Deleted members retain prior display names/filtering; new assignments validate current member IDs. Filters apply to loaded summaries and compose with existing filters. No IMAP flag, read state or email transmission changes.

Only local access-gate 401 responses carry X-Apex-Auth-Required: local. Legacy plain Authentication required and local login HTML remain supported. Integration JSON 401 and other business 4xx preserve messages without login navigation or offline fallback. Session-status still controls actual session recovery; no protected endpoint is made public.

data_source: runtime bound case folder/Stella办案成果/<task_id>/task.json
capabilities.compatibility: Additive fact-check and evidence-book workbench. Existing cases/folder bindings are the source of truth; JSON task metadata and immutable output versions live inside the bound folder. No schema migration. Validated literal quotes are AI preliminary classifications, with separate lawyer review and optimistic revision checks. Evidence booklet has independent numbering and original-page mapping, never changes case status. Shared PDF/image assembly is reused by existing archive export. Case-scoped source hashes, verified private input copies, fixed hash-checked parsed candidates and validated paths prevent stale citations and traversal. Shared PDF assembly flattens visible annotations/widgets in a private copy (PyMuPDF >=1.24.2). Workflow picker uses versioned apex:workflow-* messages; archive messages remain compatible. Heavy job execution is bounded, hidden pages stop polling, process restarts mark unfinished tasks interrupted. Document-led evidence_plan jobs reuse fact checking and carry reviewed facts by immutable task/revision. Plans persist with optimistic revisions; normalized entries accept multiple source materials, physical page selection, summary, proof purpose, optional origin/group and validated document item IDs. Compilation verifies original inputs and records actual selected-page mapping, document-to-evidence relationships and explicit gap acknowledgement. Page images are served through case/task scoped material-info, material-preview and material-page routes. Legacy one-file book requests and stopped historical tasks are normalized on load and remain resumable. Converted preview caches carry SHA-256 manifests; altered previews are rejected. Atomic worker registration and a short-lived creation reservation prevent active jobs being marked interrupted between creation and launch. The evidence editor renders one active entry with a compact directory rail while validating every entry, including inactive page ranges. Splitting material clears proof summaries/associations for renewed lawyer review. Timeline jobs reuse verified source snapshots and parser caches. Every parsed chunk is processed with checkpointed batches; literal source citations are required, date precision is retained without inferring specific days. Same-topic date differences remain review candidates. Human edits and case-scoped manual additions require review notes and optimistic revisions; immutable DOCX/XLSX/Markdown/JSON/SVG/PDF exports retain sources. No schema migration. Fact and plan review exports recheck original hashes and folder binding after generation before publication; fact exports run outside the async event loop. DOCX chronology uses a fixed-width repeated-header event table and deduplicated indexed source/quote appendix, preserving complete event text, review states and citations.
